records.statement: Architecture must be proportional to verified product, system, organizational and lifecycle needs.
Prefer the simplest reversible architecture that satisfies binding functional and non-functional requirements.
A modular monolith is the default comparison baseline before distribution; it is not an automatic final choice.
Distribution requires explicit evidence for independent deployability, isolation, differential scaling or organizational autonomy.
Reliability, scalability, maintainability, security and operability remain separate requirements and trade-offs.
Data architecture must record system of record, derived state, consistency expectations, failure modes and lineage.
An architecture decision requires context, alternatives, trade-offs, evidence, reversibility, review trigger and retirement condition.
Code review, testing, documentation, dependency management, build systems and migrations are part of solution sustainability.
Legacy changes begin by characterizing observed behavior and creating a bounded safety net before structural refactoring.
Patterns are conditional responses to specific forces and must not be accumulated as default structure.
Interview architectures and historical examples cannot establish production fitness without current project evidence.
Current security controls and claims require current primary sources and project-specific threat and data boundaries.
